messages:
Maria: Quick thought — we need a small playbook that defines the "borderline" responsibilities between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Not another huge RFC, just operational rules + example flows.
Sam: +1. can we focus on 3 concrete handoffs: auth, observability, and failover? Those are where folks keep getting tripped up. :thinking_face: 
Lee: Agree. Also include a tiny matrix: who owns cert rotation, who emits tenant metrics, and who performs KV cache invalidation on rollout.
Maria: I sketched a minimal flow for auth exchange. Idea: control-plane issues short-lived session certs for Hosted, but Private mode can opt-out and present customer-managed certs. Example: 
```
# auth hint (not prod)
POST /v1/auth/exchange
{ "src_mode": "hosted", "dest_mode": "private", "tenant": "acme" }
-> returns {"client_cert": "PEM", "expires_at": "..."}
```
Sam: That looks fine. Two concerns: 1) latency of the exchange on cold path, 2) how to recover if KMS/HSM in Private is unreachable.
Jess: For (1) we can cache the cert in the runtime for a short TTL and do async renewal. For (2) fallback policy: if private KMS unavailable, we either fail-safe (reject) or fail-open to a fallback key depending on customer tier — must be explicit in the playbook.
Lee: +1 on explicit tiers. We should capture SLO implications. If fallback-key is used, tag all outputs and surface in the Console with a red banner and audit event.
Arjun: Observability contract: every runtime must emit these three labels on traces: hosting_mode, model_variant, tenant_id. Without them downstream dashboards break. Put that in the playbook as a MUST.
Maria: Also add a small example of metric naming so alerts are portable: `inference.latency.p50.{hosting_mode}` and `inference.cost.per_token.{hosting_mode}`.
OpsBot: deploy:infra:auth-exchange v1 -> staging started by @sam at 5556667801 :rocket: 
Sam: Rollout plan note — canary on Dedicated only, then expand to Hosted. Private mode won't be auto-rolled; ops must handshake with customer. Document the manual-check checklist.
Jess: Canary checklist: verify metrics emitted, KV cache warm, circuit-breaker trips after 3 consecutive 500s, fallback to cheaper model variant on timeout (200ms).
Lee: On fallback semantics — define monotonic degradation: first degrade quantization (cheaper model), then degrade routing (region fallback), then degrade consistency (stale cache). Order matters.
Maria: Good. Also call out secret rebind race: when we rotate a secret on the control plane while Private sidecar is still using old secret. Include a debounce guidance: wait_for_consensus window of 30s and a rollback path.
Arjun: Add a short section on test harness: a tiny end-to-end script that simulates private KMS failure and asserts observability tags remain present and that fallback events are logged. Link: https://go/internal/playbooks/infer-mode-playbook 
Sam: Can someone own the doc writeup? I can do a first pass if @Maria and @Jess review.
Maria: I'll take review and add the metric examples.
Jess: I'll add the canary checklist + sample prometheus rules.
Lee: Quick Q — do we want a separate GRPC handshake for controlplane <-> runtime, or keep HTTP/JSON?
Sam: GRPC for internal controlplane for perf; keep public-facing REST. Document both flows.
Maria: Awesome. I'll push a tiny md in the playbooks dir and ping y'all. Minimal, operational, and explicit. :thumbsup:
